newsitem.title: USA: U.S. natgas industry poised for boom - analyst.
newsitem.headline: U.S. natgas industry poised for boom - analyst.

text.p: The U.S. natural gas industry is poised for a boom in the coming years as reserve growth fails to keep pace with increased production flows, First Albany Corp energy analyst Michael Smolinski said on Friday.

Domestic natural gas prices could hit $5.00 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) in the time frame of the years 2002 to 2007 as producers step up drilling to boost both the flow rate and reserve base, Smolinski said in Houston at an International Association of Drilling Contractors meeting.

Smolinski compared the industry's outlook to boom years between 1973 and 1984, when natural gas prices surged from $0.23 mmBtu to $2.64 mmBtu. "We're looking at a similar cycle, but nowhere near the magnitude of price increases," he said.

In the near term, the Boston-based analyst expects U.S. natural gas prices to hit $3.00 mmBtu by November 1 and move into the $3.80 mmBtu range in January or February, with possible price spikes fueled by severe weather.

"The market is tighter, but (gas) is better distributed" compared to last year, said Smolinski, who sees early winter inventory levels of 2,700 to 2,750 billion cubic feet, down from 2,958 bcf in storage at the same time last year and 3,099 bcf in storage before the onset of winter the year before.
